questions.question: To reduce genu recurvatum with an ankle-foot orthosis, the ankle should be set in:

options.A: A few degrees of plantar flexion

questions.explanation: Plantar flexion stop creates a flexion moment at the knee.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Kisner & Colby; Tidy's Physiotherapy; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: If an AFO is set in excessive dorsiflexion, during stance the patient will tend to show:
questions.explanation: Dorsiflexion pushes the tibia forward over the foot.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Kisner & Colby; Tidy's Physiotherapy; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A knee–ankle–foot orthosis (KAFO) is indicated when there is:

questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Kisner & Colby; Tidy's Physiotherapy; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A hip–knee–ankle–foot orthosis (HKAFO) is used for:

options.B: Paraplegia with trunk and hip weakness

questions.explanation: Reciprocating gait orthosis (RGO) is a type.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Kisner & Colby; Tidy's Physiotherapy; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A Thomas (soft) collar is used to:

questions.question: The Boston brace is a:

questions.question: A Taylor brace restricts:

questions.question: A hinged knee brace after ACL reconstruction is designed to:

questions.question: A resting hand splint for rheumatoid arthritis holds the hand in:

questions.question: A dynamic splint differs from a static splint in that it:

options.B: Includes elastic or spring components that allow controlled movement or assist motion

questions.explanation: Used in radial nerve palsy (lively splint).

questions.question: A heel cup or heel pad is used in:

options.A: Heel pain such as plantar fasciitis

questions.question: A metatarsal bar or pad is used to:
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Kisner & Colby; Tidy's Physiotherapy; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A shoe raise is used to correct:
questions.explanation: A discrepancy over 1 cm is usually treated.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Kisner & Colby; Tidy's Physiotherapy; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A SACH foot is a prosthetic foot with:

questions.question: A Syme's amputation is:

questions.question: The ideal length of a below-knee residual limb is about:

options.A: 12–15 cm below the knee joint line

questions.explanation: A tibial length of at least 12 cm is recommended.

questions.question: Residual limb shrinking is encouraged by:
questions.explanation: Reduces oedema and shapes the limb for prosthetic fitting.

questions.question: An immediate post-operative prosthesis (IPOP) is applied:

questions.question: Phantom limb sensation after amputation is:

questions.question: A neuroma at the end of a residual limb causes:

questions.question: A prosthesis for hip disarticulation includes a:

questions.question: A prosthetic knee unit that locks only when weight is applied is a:
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Kisner & Colby; Tidy's Physiotherapy; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Suspension of a transtibial prosthesis can be achieved by:

questions.question: In bandaging a below-knee residual limb, the bandage should be applied:

options.D: Diagonally with greatest pressure distally and including the knee joint

questions.question: Circumduction of a transfemoral prosthesis during swing may result from:

options.A: A prosthesis that is too short only
options.B: A prosthesis that is too long or a stiff knee, or fear of knee flexion

questions.question: An abducted gait in a transfemoral amputee may be caused by:

questions.question: Lateral trunk bending toward the prosthetic side during stance in a transfemoral amputee suggests:

options.B: Weak hip abductors, a short prosthesis or a high lateral wall

questions.explanation: Similar to a gluteus medius lurch.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Kisner & Colby; Tidy's Physiotherapy; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Compared with a below-knee amputee, an above-knee amputee uses:
questions.explanation: Increases with a more proximal level of amputation.

questions.question: A body-powered upper limb prosthesis uses:

questions.question: A myoelectric prosthesis is controlled by:

questions.question: In a diabetic amputee, care of the remaining foot is important because:

questions.question: A functional brace (Sarmiento) for tibial or humeral fractures allows:
